messages:
Sam: quick heads-up — ran a 48h long-context soak on the dedicated A100 pool. KV cache resident size climbs ~8-12% over time and never properly plateaus. Hosted pool for the same workload stays stable, private onprem shows repeated spikes then drops. attaching minimal profiler dump below

Olivia: can you paste the growth numbers and kernel info? was there a change in kernel selection across pools?

Sam: yeah here are the two samples (trimmed):
```
dedicated: kv_resident_mb=12480 -> 14032 (+12.5%) over 48h, kernel=attn_opt_v2, driver=515.76
hosted:    kv_resident_mb=12510 -> 12600 (+0.7%)  over 48h, kernel=attn_opt_v1, driver=525.30
onprem:    kv_resident_mb=12390 -> 13600 (+9.8%)  over 48h, kernel=attn_opt_v2, driver=510.39
```
NOTICE: dedicated and onprem picked v2 kernels; hosted stuck on v1 (fallback) due to a driver/lib mismatch.

Jia: hmm interesting. v2 changed the KV backfill scheduling last quarter (smaller page refs before async evict). Could be a backfill vs reuse tradeoff. Any differences in vm settings or hugepages across those envs?

Sam: checked — hosted has vm.nr_hugepages=0, jemalloc background thread enabled. Dedicated had hugepages disabled too but we run with a private cgroup mem limit (container memory=384GB) and cgroup swap=0. Onprem uses standard hugepages=2048 for GPU nodes.

Ryan: another angle: batching heuristics changed in the runtime a week ago — auto-batch window shortened on hosted to meet 50ms p95, that reduces the continuous KV reuse window (requests less likely to coalesce) which *should* reduce growth, not increase it. So growth on dedicated implies something else (maybe delayed eviction/backfill).

Sam: exactly — my hypothesis: attn_opt_v2 reduces per-token kernel memory but moved more state into long-lived KV frames and made async backfill slower. On dedicated we also saw more fragmented page allocations in resident set (high page_count but lower contiguous runs). When async evict/backfill is slower, we get steady accumulation until a large GC sweep, but our GC cadence is tuned for hosted defaults.

Olivia: do we have jemalloc profiling (alloc/dump) from the nodes? fragmentation metrics would help (dirty pages, rss vs anon).

Sam: posted a small jemalloc snapshot from dedicated: rss=410GB, anon=390GB, mapped=22GB, dirty=6GB, page_holes=~12k. On hosted rss ~392GB, anon=378GB, dirty=3GB, page_holes=~1.2k. So dedicated has way more page holes.

Jia: VPC/network differences could explain on-hosted being more conservative w/ kernel selection. Also cgroup OOM behavior can prevent timely page reclamation. If dedicated has a tighter cgroup mem limit, the runtime might avoid eager reclaim to prevent latency spikes. Could be policy-level.

Ryan: runtime has per-deployment eviction policy override in config: `kv.eviction.max_live_pages` and `kv.backfill.rate`. Can you check values used across envs?

Sam: found them:
```
hosted:   kv.eviction.max_live_pages=60000, kv.backfill.rate=0.35
dedicated:kv.eviction.max_live_pages=120000, kv.backfill.rate=0.12
onprem:   kv.eviction.max_live_pages=90000, kv.backfill.rate=0.18
```
Weird — dedicated uses much higher max_live_pages and a low backfill.rate. That aligns with observed growth. Seems like a config drift landed during the dedicated rollout.

Olivia: aha — that explains it. Higher max_live_pages + slower backfill = more resident pages before eviction kicks. Why was this policy set higher for dedicated?

Sam: looks like an opt-in from Dedicated perf tuning around 2025-11 to favor throughput under sustained throughput tests. It was never reconciled with the newer attn_opt_v2 semantics.

Jia: action: run a short experiment on dedicated where we (1) set kv.backfill.rate=0.4 and kv.eviction.max_live_pages=65000, (2) force kernel selection to attn_opt_v1 via runtime flag, (3) enable jemalloc arena decay tuning to speed fragmentation coalescing. Compare 24h.

Ryan: +1. Also add a trace to track page coalescing events and backfill window sizes (we have a perf tracepoint already: runtime.kv.backfill_event). Can infra-bot schedule a canary?

infra-bot: scheduled canary job `kvcache-slow-backfill-canary` on dedicated pool: start=3067891200, duration=24h. Notifying eng-runtime on completion.

Sam: thanks — I'll also post the reproduction steps and attach the jemalloc heap profile. If this fixes it, we should rollout a config alignment job to reconcile dedicated/private/hosted defaults and add a guard in the deploy pipeline to block `kv.eviction.*` changes without eval.

Olivia: sounds good. last ask: add an entry in the perf-regressions board linking kernel version + eviction params so we don't regress when we bump kernels.

Sam: on it. I opened GH issue #INF-4121 with the dump and steps. Will share results after the canary completes. :thumbsup:
